The '''2007–08 Scottish Premier League''' season was the tenth season of the [[Scottish Premier League]]. It began on 4 August 2007 and was originally due to end on 18 May 2008. Due to the death of [[Phil O'Donnell (footballer)|Phil O'Donnell]] and extremely poor weather causing the postponement of fixtures during the winter, as well as a backlog of [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] fixtures and their progression to the [[2008 UEFA Cup Final|UEFA Cup Final]], the SPL decided to move the final round of fixtures back four days to 22 May 2008.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/7360790.stm|title=SPL prepares for season extension|date=22 April 2008|via=news.bbc.co.uk}}</ref> It was the first season under the sponsorship of the [[Clydesdale Bank]].

[[Gretna F.C.|Gretna]] had been promoted from the First Division and played in the SPL for the first time, replacing [[Dunfermline Athletic F.C.|Dunfermline Athletic]]. Gretna did not play at their home stadium [[Raydale Park]] as it did not meet the SPL stadia criteria of 6,000 and instead used [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]]'s [[Fir Park]] for all but one of their games; that match was at [[Livingston F.C.|Livingston]]'s [[Almondvale Stadium]].

The championship was determined on the final day of the season with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and Rangers even on 86 points. Celtic travelled to [[Tannadice Park|Tannadice]] to play [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] knowing that a win would likely secure the title due to their superior goal difference (+57 to +53). Meanwhile, Rangers needed to better Celtic's result in their match against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] at [[Pittodrie Stadium|Pittodrie]] (or in the event of both winning, overhaul the goal difference). As it turned out, Celtic won 1–0 following [[Jan Vennegoor of Hesselink]]'s second-half header, while Aberdeen beat Rangers 2–0 thanks to goals from [[Lee Miller (footballer)|Lee Miller]] and [[Steve Lovell]].

Celtic qualified directly for the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], while second-placed Rangers qualified for the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League#Second qualifying round|Second qualifying round]]. Third-placed Motherwell qualified for the [[2008–09 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]] and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] qualified for the [[2008 UEFA Intertoto Cup|Intertoto Cup]]. [[Scottish Football League First Division|First Division]] side [[Queen of the South F.C.|Queen of the South]] also qualified for the UEFA Cup after reaching the [[2008 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup Final]], losing to Rangers. Gretna were [[promotion and relegation|relegated]] after just one season in the SPL and were replaced by First Division champions [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] for the [[2008–09 Scottish Premier League|following season]].

==Notable events==
{{main article|2007–08 in Scottish football}}

*'''29 December:''' Thirty-five-year-old [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] captain [[Phil O'Donnell (footballer)|Phil O'Donnell]] collapsed on the pitch at [[Fir Park]] during a match against [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], and died later that evening.<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/m/motherwell/7164150.stm Motherwell captain O'Donnell dies] ''BBC Sport''. Retrieved 29 December 2007</ref>
*'''29 March:''' [[Gretna F.C.|Gretna]] were relegated after losing 2–0 to [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] at [[Love Street (stadium)|Love Street]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/7317663.stm|work=[[BBC Sport]]|title= St Mirren 2-0 Gretna|date=29 March 2008|access-date=29 March 2008}}</ref>
*'''19 April:''' [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] won promotion to the [[Scottish Premier League]] as [[Scottish First Division|First Division]] champions following a 2–0 over [[Clyde F.C.|Clyde]].<ref name="Hamilton Accies 2-0 Clyde">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_div_1/7353608.stm|work=[[BBC Sport]]|title=Hamilton Accies 2-0 Clyde|date=19 April 2008|access-date=19 April 2008}}</ref>
*'''22 May:''' [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] won their third successive SPL title after defeating [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] 1–0.<ref name=" Dundee United 0-1 Celtic">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_prem/7412454.stm|work=[[BBC Sport]]|title=Dundee United 0-1 Celtic|date=22 May 2008|access-date=22 May 2008}}</ref>
*'''29 May:''' [[Gretna F.C.|Gretna]] were demoted to the [[Scottish Football League Third Division|Third Division]] after administrator David Elliot could not guarantee the Football League that the club would fulfil its fixtures next season.<ref name=" Gretna demoted to Division Three">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/g/gretna/7426281.stm|work=[[BBC Sport]]|title= Gretna demoted to Division Three|date=29 May 2008|access-date=29 May 2008}}</ref>
*'''2 June:''' [[Gretna F.C.|Gretna]] resigned from the Scottish Football League because the administrator concluded that the club could not continue to run as a business.<ref name=resign>{{cite news|title=Gretna resign from Scottish Football League|url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/scotland/article4057942.ece|newspaper=The Times|date=2 June 2008|access-date=2 June 2008 | location=London}}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

|note_res_IC=[[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] qualified for the [[2008 UEFA Intertoto Cup|Intertoto Cup]] as the highest ranked club to apply for a place in the competition.
|note_res_REL=At the end of the season, [[Gretna F.C.|Gretna]] were relegated to the [[Scottish Third Division|Third Division]] due to their financial struggles. However, as no buyer was found for the club, they resigned from the [[Scottish Football League]] and were subsequently [[Liquidation|liquidated]].
}}</onlyinclude>

==Broadcasting rights==
[[Setanta Sports]] provided domestic TV live coverage and highlights as in previous seasons, with [[STV (TV network)|STV]] and [[BBC Scotland]] also broadcasting free-to-air highlights. [[BBC Radio Scotland]] continued to provide domestic radio coverage, with many games also available internationally, and all domestically, through their website. The [[BBC]] held rights to show highlights online and do so through the BBC Sport website. Internationally, the Premier League's overseas television broadcasting partner was [[Trans World International#Trans World International|TWI]], with coverage of the SPL available in over 100 territories worldwide.[https://web.archive.org/web/20070805061745/http://www.scotprem.premiumtv.co.uk/page/Overseas/0,,10002,00.html Overseas Broadcasting | Scottish Premier League | Broadcasting | Overseas]
